authority: National Record-Clearing Legal Decision Report, current through 2026-08-28 (docs/record-clearing/NATIONAL_LEGAL_DECISION_REPORT_2026-08-28.md, sha256 84ef2b61126aa26cd66dec5dfb39a112d87c5a92397ab92efd452cc1e5ad1336). Kept as its own batch so this authority can be reverted alone, and so a reader can tell which decisions came from the report rather than from the 2026-08-24 decision matrix.

routes.mechanism: Pretrial intervention expungement, administered by the solicitor

timing.anchorText: the solicitor's office administers the expungement on successful completion of pretrial intervention; the participant files no pleading and sits through no elapsed wait

requiredFacts: Which solicitor's circuit administered the intervention program?
Was the program successfully completed, and is completion documented?
Has the solicitor's office issued or refused the expungement?
Is eligibility contested by the solicitor?
exclusions: Successful completion of the intervention program is required
A solicitor denial or contested eligibility leaves the ordinary route entirely

items: the circuit-specific solicitor application form or intake instruction
the payee named by that circuit for the administrative fee
the delivery method and address that circuit requires
deliveryGates.evidenceReference: pending: no circuit configuration record exists yet
deliveryGates.note: The statewide rule is settled; what is missing is per-circuit administrative detail. This gate holds the guidance content, not the legal answer.

failureDisposition.note: A denied application is individualized advocacy, not a self-help filing. This is a service disposition, not missing statewide research.

failureDisposition.when: eligibility is contested by the solicitor
failureDisposition.note: A contested eligibility question leaves the ordinary route entirely.

commercialPosture.note: Guidance is never sold and never consumes a sponsored credit. Declared to state the posture explicitly; the derived payment authority closes it regardless.

supersedes.note: The rescinded $150 single-incident administrative figure. It must not appear anywhere on this route.

routes.notes: Report correction 4. The ordinary PTI custom participant pleading is RETIRED: the solicitor's office administers the process, so the product's output is process guidance and intake support and never a generated pleading. The controlling figures for guidance content are a $250 solicitor administrative fee, a $0 SLED verification fee, a $35 clerk filing fee where one applies, and a $285 ordinary total on that combination. Those figures belong to THIS route only: the report resolves the obsolete-$150 question across the other seven South Carolina routes, but each of those keeps its own statutory exemptions and its own fees, and this schedule must not be copied onto them.

routes.mechanism: Automatic non-conviction court-record closing, with verification and correction

timing.anchorText: the court closes the record by operation of the statute; the participant waits 61 complete days from the qualifying disposition, verifies on day 62 or the next business day, and files nothing to obtain the closure itself

processingDeadlines.label: 61 complete days from the qualifying disposition, then verify on day 62 or the next business day
processingDeadlines.note: The court's own implementation period, not a participant eligibility wait. Nothing is filed during it and nothing the participant does shortens it.

requiredFacts: What was the qualifying non-conviction disposition, and on what exact date? (nd_qualifying_disposition_date, confirmed against the authenticated record at final verification rather than recalled in screening)
Was that disposition entered on or after 2025-08-01?
Does the case still appear on the public index on day 62?
Has the clerk of the original court been asked in writing to implement the closure?
Does the criminal history held by BCI or the originating agency still show the matter?
Is eligibility contested?
exclusions: A qualifying non-conviction disposition is required
No individualized notice may be promised: neither the statute nor the official publications say the participant is told the record was closed
Contested eligibility is an attorney handoff, not a self-help filing

serviceBranches.when: the qualifying disposition was entered before 2025-08-01
serviceBranches.packetFamily: North Dakota § 12-60.1-05 Petition and Proposed Order

commercialPosture.note: This branch is a real participant filing, so its posture is its own rather than the automatic parent's. It stays closed today because its artifact gate is open, not because the branch forbids selling.

serviceBranches.note: Before the amendment took effect the record does not close by operation of law, so the participant files the official petition and proposed order. The artifact does not exist yet, so this branch resolves to identified-but-not-yet-available. It must never be served the post-2025 verification guidance as though that were the completed outcome: the record will not close on its own and the participant would wait for something that never happens.

serviceBranches.when: the qualifying disposition was entered on or after 2025-08-01
serviceBranches.note: The record closes by operation of the statute. Wait 61 complete days from the qualifying disposition, verify on day 62 or the next business day, and file nothing to obtain the closure itself.

failureDisposition.when: the record still appears on the public index on day 62
failureDisposition.note: First a written request to the clerk of the original court to implement the closure. If the clerk cannot correct it, a motion to enforce in the original criminal case.

failureDisposition.when: the BCI or originating-agency criminal history still shows the matter after the court record is closed
failureDisposition.note: A separate challenge to BCI or the originating agency. Closing the court record does not correct an agency history, and the two must not be presented as one step.

failureDisposition.when: eligibility for the automatic closure is contested
failureDisposition.note: A contested eligibility question is individualized advocacy.

items: the official pre-2025-08-01 petition and proposed order for the pre_effective_date_petition branch
deliveryGates.evidenceReference: pending: no rendered candidate exists yet
deliveryGates.note: Scoped to the pre-effective-date branch by id. It must not hold the post-2025-08-01 default, which is guidance and needs no artifact.

commercialPosture.note: Relief happens by operation of law on the default branch, so nothing is sold. The pre-effective-date branch is not built, so nothing is sold there either.

routes.notes: Report correction 3. For a disposition on or after 2025-08-01 the initial output is guidance and verification, never a routine petition: the record closes by operation of law and filing a petition asks a court to do what the statute already did. The exact disposition date is a route-resolution fact confirmed at final verification, not a screening estimate: it decides which statute governs, and an approximate date selects the wrong branch. With the date absent the route resolves to needs-more-info rather than defaulting to either branch. CONTRACT MODEL: option B, branch-specific stage and commercial posture, chosen over two contracts. The routeKey is JURISDICTION:pathwayId and the compiled profile models this as one pathway, so two contracts would require inventing a second pathwayId for what is one statute at two points in its legislative history. The split is temporal, not mechanistic, which is what a branch is for; a second statute would need a second contract.

routes.mechanism: Expungement of a first § 311.325 minor-in-possession conviction, filed as a new miscellaneous civil matter

timing.anchorText: not less than one year after the person's twenty-first birthday

requiredFacts: Is the judgment expressly under Mo. Rev. Stat. § 311.325, or under a county or municipal ordinance?
If an ordinance, does it expressly adopt the § 311.326 remedy, or does it merely mirror the substantive offence?
Date of birth and date the person turned twenty-one?
Which circuit court sentenced the person, and in which division?
What is the original criminal case number and judgment?
Any later alcohol-related offence?
Did the person hold a commercial driver's licence or operate a commercial motor vehicle?
exclusions: A later alcohol-related offence defeats the application
Eligibility turns on the actual statute or ordinance of conviction, never on the shorthand offence label
packetComponents: Reference to the original criminal case, judgment and sentencing division
Certified disposition where the judgment is ambiguous

serviceBranches.when: the judgment is expressly under Mo. Rev. Stat. § 311.325
serviceBranches.note: The state route. Section 311.326 refers throughout to a violation of § 311.325 and does not carry the broader language used elsewhere to reach substantially similar county or municipal ordinances.

serviceBranches.when: a local ordinance expressly adopts the § 311.326 remedy
serviceBranches.note: Express local adoption may create a separate local-law route. That is a different route under a different instrument, and this contract does not carry it: the participant is referred to local-law review rather than served the state petition.

serviceBranches.when: the ordinance merely mirrors the substantive offence without adopting the remedy
serviceBranches.note: Not automatically within § 311.326. Mere equivalence of the substantive offence does not bring an ordinance conviction inside a statute that names § 311.325. Assess § 610.140 or local relief instead.

serviceBranches.when: the judgment does not state clearly which instrument it was entered under
serviceBranches.note: Obtain the certified disposition and hold for local-law review. Guessing the instrument from an offence label is the error the exclusion names.

items: the final caption the receiving circuit clerk accepts for a § 311.326 application
deliveryGates.evidenceReference: pending: no receiving-clerk configuration record exists yet
deliveryGates.note: The configurable default is 'In the Matter of the Application of [Name] for Expungement Under § 311.326, RSMo'. It is a default, not a confirmed caption.

items: the FI-05 case-type code the receiving clerk directs: XG provisional, X5 prohibited, X1 only on clerk direction
deliveryGates.note: FI-05 is a confidential case-filing information sheet, not itself a case-type code. XG is the provisional generic code; X5 is never used by analogy because its published description ties it to § 610.140; X1 only where the receiving clerk directs it.

items: the filing fee the receiving circuit charges for a new miscellaneous civil expungement matter
deliveryGates.note: No statewide figure is published for this filing model.

items: the service documents and method the receiving circuit requires
deliveryGates.note: Section 311.326 prescribes no statewide respondent list or service method.

items: whether the receiving circuit issues a summons on this filing model, and on what form
deliveryGates.note: A new miscellaneous civil matter may or may not draw a summons depending on the circuit.

items: the division instructions linking the new matter to the original criminal case and sentencing division
deliveryGates.note: The petition identifies the original case, judgment and sentencing division; how the clerk links them is local practice.

failureDisposition.when: the conviction is under an ordinance that merely mirrors the offence
failureDisposition.note: Assess § 610.140 or local relief. This route does not reach the conviction.

failureDisposition.when: the judgment is ambiguous as to the instrument of conviction
failureDisposition.note: Obtain the certified disposition from the sentencing court, then re-resolve.

commercialPosture.note: The merits petition is a real participant filing and is sellable in principle. It stays closed today because six receiving-clerk configuration gates are open, not because the route forbids selling.

routes.notes: Report correction 2, LA-IMM-02. The merits petition is built; the clerk-confirmation gate is operational configuration, NOT unresolved legal research, and must never be sent to counsel as though it were. The absence of a dedicated case-type code does not defeat the statutory remedy; it prevents releasing universal administrative instructions without a clerk-practice gate. This decision is scoped to § 311.326 and must not be extended to mo-610-130 or any other Missouri route without its own evidence.

routes.mechanism: Petition for retroactive First Offender treatment, exoneration and discharge

timing.anchorText: available once written prosecutorial consent exists; § 42-8-66 imposes no elapsed wait and no filing fee

requiredFacts: Does the participant hold the prosecuting attorney's WRITTEN consent, joinder or signed endorsement?
In which court was the conviction entered?
What are the original case number, judgment, sentence and disposition?
Was the participant eligible for First Offender treatment at the time?
Which § 42-8-66 branch applies?
Is there any prior felony or prior First Offender history?
Has a qualifying order already been granted, and on what date?
exclusions: Written prosecutorial consent is a filing prerequisite, not the relief itself
A phone call, an unanswered request, prosecutor silence or 'no known objection' is not written consent
Consent withdrawn before the order is entered defeats the filing
A contested evidentiary hearing leaves self-help
packetComponents: Petition for retroactive First Offender treatment, exoneration and discharge
Written prosecutor consent, joinder or signed consent endorsement
Certificate of service or local notice document
Evidence of original First Offender eligibility
Post-order restriction, sealing and verification instructions

packetReleasePreconditions.requires: verified written prosecutorial consent, joinder or signed consent endorsement, held as a document
packetReleasePreconditions.note: O.C.G.A. § 42-8-66 makes consent a condition that must exist BEFORE the individual files. Absence is never satisfaction: silence, refusal, an unanswered request and 'no known objection' each leave the precondition unmet, and each produces an attorney or prosecutor handoff rather than a petition. Collected at authenticated intake and proved at final verification against the document itself, never in anonymous screening.

serviceBranches.when: a qualifying order was granted on or after 2026-07-01

commercialPosture.note: The court has already granted the relief. There is nothing to petition for and nothing to sell.

serviceBranches.note: For a retroactive discharge entered on or after 1 July 2026 the proposed order expressly addresses the current restriction and court-record sealing duties. The product becomes restriction, sealing, agency distribution and verification tracking. Generating a second merits petition would ask the court to grant what it has already granted.

serviceBranches.when: a qualifying order was granted before 2026-07-01

commercialPosture.note: Relief already granted. Implementation and verification only.

serviceBranches.note: An order already granted is not re-petitioned whatever its date. The route is implementation and verification.

failureDisposition.note: Refusal is not a defect in the packet; it is the absence of the statutory prerequisite. The matter goes to an attorney or back to the prosecutor.
Consent withdrawn before the order is entered defeats the filing.

failureDisposition.when: the court requires a contested evidentiary hearing
failureDisposition.note: A contested evidentiary hearing is advocacy, not document preparation.

commercialPosture.note: A real participant petition, sellable once verified written consent exists. The consent precondition, not the posture, is what holds it closed.

routes.notes: Report correction 1, LA-IMM-01. Venue is the court of conviction; the default docket is the original criminal case, preserved unless the receiving clerk requires an ancillary number. The statute imposes no filing fee. The route name matters: § 42-8-66 is NOT limited to youthful offenders, so the legacy pathway id youthful-first-offender-restriction-route misdescribes it. That legacy id is preserved and aliased rather than renamed, because renaming a stored pathway identifier without a complete dependency migration would break saved matters and fixtures.
